text:
Sam Chen: quick heads-up — Acme Health POC hitting intermittent 429s and traces aren't linking to logs in the console. customer says 'requests look fine on our side'.
Priya Patel: thanks — do we have an example request/trace id from them? need one to correlate on our side.
Ava Ramirez: they sent this header example: `X-Redwood-Trace: 8a7f3b4e-2c1d-11ee-8c99-0242ac120002` and a curl: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Redwood-Trace: 8a7f3b4e-2c1d-11ee-8c99-0242ac120002' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat`
Jordan Lee: can you ask them to repro with DEBUG logging enabled? set `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug` and capture the agent logs. that will show prefix/correlation and 429 reason.
Sam Chen: they ran debug and attached a snippet: `2026-03-05T18:12:04Z INFO request id=8a7f3b4e trace=8a7f3b4e route=/v1/chat status=429 reason="rate_limit"` — so request shows 429 at our edge but no span id in Console traces.
Priya Patel: two possibilities: 1) the trace header isn't propagated into the internal span (config issue) 2) the log exporter didn't include trace metadata. quick test: ask them to include `X-Redwood-Span: <span-id>` OR we can enable automatic span injection from the console for the POC.
Ava Ramirez: Can we enable span injection for their dedicated token? what's the exact console toggle?
Jordan Lee: Console -> Settings -> Observability -> "Auto-attach trace id to logs" (dev/test only) — toggle, then restart agent or redeploy client. Alternatively, they can use the SDK helper: `redwood.sdk.attach_trace()` to force attach.
Sam Chen: did that on a staging token and repro — after toggling, logs show: `2026-03-05T18:12:04Z INFO request id=8a7f3b4e trace=8a7f3b4e span=3c9d... route=/v1/chat status=200` good.
Priya Patel: next: exporting logs/traces to their Splunk/S3. For Splunk we recommend using the log-forwarder: enable "Log Sink" in Console -> Exports -> Add -> Splunk HEC (token, url). For S3, add role arn and prefix and set format to json_with_trace.
Ava Ramirez: they asked about keeping trace ids when we batch requests (batching causes new internal request ids). Answer: we include original `X-Redwood-Trace` as `orig_trace_id` in batched envelope and it gets expanded back into individual spans. share the snippet: ```json
{
  "envelope": {
    "orig_trace_id": "8a7f3b4e-2c1d-11ee-8c99-0242ac120002",
    "requests": [ ... ]
  }
}
```
Jordan Lee: one more POC blocker: they saw missing events in the Console timeline during concurrency bursts. likely a buffering threshold in the forwarder. workaround: reduce client batch window to 10ms or raise `REDWOOD_FORWARDER_BUFFER_MB` to 64.
Sam Chen: confirmed raising buffer fixed the missing events in our internal repro. sent instructions to customer.
Ava Ramirez: also filed a small internal ticket to add clearer docs: "How trace ids are preserved through batching & forwarding" so future POCs won't be blocked.
TelemetryBot: export job started for AcmeHealth-poc -> s3://acme-poc-redwood-logs/ part=0001 status=ok
Sam Chen: great — follow-up action items: 1) Priya to validate Splunk HEC export with customer credentials, 2) Jordan to add a console helper script to toggle span injection for POCs, 3) Ava to send the buffer + env variable steps in the POC runbook.
Priya Patel: on it, will DM creds and run a quick end-to-end. :thumbsup:
Jordan Lee: i'll draft the helper and post in eng-oncall channel when ready.
Ava Ramirez: I'll update the doc and ping the sales AE with a one-pager.
Sam Chen: thanks team — marking this thread resolved for now, will re-open if they hit further 429s or missing traces. :white_check_mark:
